summary: This Dockerfile creates a Ubuntu container with ripgrep (a fast search tool) and zsh shell configured for development. It sets up custom search functions to find TODOs and environment variables, then populates a demo project with PHP, JavaScript, and configuration files to showcase the search capabilities.

explanations.3: DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive tells the package installer not to ask interactive questions during installation, so the build won't hang waiting for user input.
explanations.5: The && chains commands together so they all run as one step; if any command fails, the rest won't execute. The backslash continues the command to the next line for readability.
explanations.11: After installing packages, we delete the apt cache files to shrink the final image size — we don't need them anymore since we won't be installing additional packages later.
explanations.14: printf '%s\n' outputs each string argument on its own line, which is a compact way to write multiple lines of text to a file.
explanations.30: The > redirects all that output to create the ripgreprc config file in /root, which is the home directory for the root user.
explanations.33: mkdir -p creates the directory and any missing parent directories (-p means it won't error if the directory already exists).
explanations.38: The ${1:-.} syntax means 'use the first argument passed to this function, or default to the current directory (.) if no argument was given'.
explanations.47: [[ -z "${var}" ]] checks if the var variable is empty; if it is, we print usage instructions and return 1 (an error code).
explanations.48: The --type-add flag lets ripgrep recognize new file patterns, so we're telling it that .env, .cfg, .ini, and .conf files should all count as 'config' type files for searching.
explanations.55: This zsh command sources (loads) every .zsh file in ~/.zsh/fns, which makes the custom functions available whenever you start a new shell.
explanations.60: The >> appends to the file instead of overwriting it, so we're adding these lines to an existing .zshrc rather than replacing it.
explanations.65: mkdir -p creates nested directories in one command; -p makes it safe to use even if some directories already exist.
explanations.79: git init -q initializes a git repository with -q (quiet mode) so it doesn't print status messages.
explanations.80: git -c sets temporary config values just for this one command: the email and name needed to create a commit.
explanations.90: CMD specifies the default command to run when the container starts; -i makes it interactive and -l makes it a login shell so it loads your config files.
